topics.description: Overview of the guiding principles and goals of the Data Science course.
Fundamentals of the R programming language used throughout the course.
High-level survey of the types of problems addressed in Data Science.
Algebraic representation and operations on vectors in n-dimensional space.
Structure, types, and basic operations of matrices.
Rules and applications of multiplying matrices with vectors.
Definition and computation of matrix rank and its implications.
The set of vectors mapped to zero by a matrix and its significance.
Systems with more equations than unknowns and their approximate solutions.
Generalized matrix inverse used to solve over-determined or singular systems.
Geometric interpretation of vectors as directions and magnitudes in space.
Geometric measures of distance between vectors and points.
Projecting one vector onto another and its geometric meaning.
Scalar values representing how a matrix scales its eigenvectors.
Vectors whose direction is unchanged under a linear transformation.
Factoring a matrix into eigenvalues and eigenvectors for analysis.
Summarizing and describing the main features of a dataset.
Foundational rules and concepts governing likelihood of events.
Functions describing how probabilities are distributed over outcomes.
The arithmetic average as a measure of central tendency.
Measure of spread indicating how far values deviate from the mean.
Measure of the joint variability between two random variables.
Matrix capturing pairwise covariances among multiple variables.
The bell-curve distribution for a single continuous random variable.
Generalization of the normal distribution to multiple correlated variables.
Statistical framework for making decisions based on data evidence.
Range of values likely to contain a population parameter with a given probability.
Introduction to the concept of finding optimal solutions to mathematical problems.
Formulation and structure of problems involving minimization or maximization.
Methods such as gradient descent used to solve optimization problems.
Categorization of common Data Science problems by their optimization structure.
Systematic approach for framing and solving Data Science problems.
Modeling the relationship between one predictor and a continuous outcome.
Key statistical assumptions required for valid linear regression results.
Diagnostic techniques to check whether regression assumptions are satisfied.
Extending linear regression to model outcomes using multiple predictors.
Evaluating regression model quality using metrics like R² and RMSE.
Determining which predictors contribute most to the regression model.
Techniques for selecting the best subset of predictors for a regression model.
Introduction to supervised learning tasks that predict categorical outcomes.
A probabilistic model for binary classification using the logistic function.
Using predicted probabilities to assign class labels to observations.
The threshold or surface separating predicted classes in feature space.
Instance-based learning algorithm that classifies points by majority vote of neighbors.
Metrics such as Euclidean distance used to identify nearest neighbors.
Strategies for selecting the optimal number of neighbors to balance bias and variance.
Applying the kNN algorithm to classify new observations from training data.
Grouping data points into clusters based on similarity without labeled data.
Learning patterns from data without predefined labels or outcomes.
Iterative algorithm that partitions data into k clusters by minimizing intra-cluster variance.
The mean position of all points in a cluster, updated iteratively in k-Means.
Assigning each data point to the nearest centroid during k-Means iterations.
Methods such as the elbow method to determine the optimal value of k.
